A.observations:
0 plain-background frames in 11 valid full-board endings (6 RM ON, 5 RM OFF). Every frame of every recording between the last cell and the results was analysed (VFR mp4 frame table plus a per-frame seek).

RM ON (6 of 6): the board→results change is always a smooth 4-5-frame crossfade (about 55-145 ms), starting 168-269 ms after the results mount.

RM OFF (5 runs) shows 3 different shapes:
- 2 smooth crossfades (rmoff1, rmoff5)
- 2 one-frame hard cuts (rmoff2, rmoff4)
- 1 fade that stalls at about 50% for 91 ms and then cuts (rmoff3)

In every cut, the first results frame has the old game screen already gone and the new content only partly opaque: the hero at about 50-70%, nothing else, and the ambient digits visible (bg 0.945-0.953). If the hero were at 0% in that frame, it would be exactly the reported plain-bg frame. The cut runs had a long gap from mount to transition (305, 526/617 and 857 ms); the smooth ones had 168-269 ms.

framestats (UI-thread stages, ms):
- rmon1 around the mount: 34.079 anim 60 + layout 16; 34.090 vsync-late 78, total 132; 34.190 draw 39, total 150; 34.401 draw 52 + RenderThread issue 27.5, total 123. The video shows no new frame for 269 ms (33.882→34.151).
- rmoff2: 07.995 anim 52, total 82; then every frame 08.017-08.262 is 44-137 ms (08.062 draw 36, total 137), and the cut comes right after.

logcat (filtered to the app pid and to WindowManager, ActivityTaskManager, SurfaceView, BLAST and Choreographer):
- In all 11 runs there are 0 lines with relaunch, configuration change, surfaceCreated or surfaceDestroyed, and no window add/remove around the end.
- Only the ambient SurfaceView's BufferQueueProducer fps line shows. 'dumpsys SurfaceFlinger --list' shows a single SurfaceView (the ambient one).
- Around each mount: 'StatusBarModule: Ignored status bar change' (about 40 ms after initGoToTop), a background GC (paused 1-6 ms, total 100-200 ms), and in RM-off runs 'ReactNativeJNI: instanceHandle is null, event of type topSvgLayout will be dropped' about 300 ms after the cut (the game screen's views are already removed).
- No 'Davey!' or 'Skipped frames' from the app. The 'Skipped N frames' lines in the rmoff3/rmoff4 logs come from other pids.
- No JS log lines: this release logs only the startup line, which was outside the windows.

Caveats:
- In rmoff2/rmoff3 my framestats dump fell 235-292 ms after the mount, close to the cut. rmoff4 cut with no dump nearby, so the cut is not caused by the measurement.
- With RM OFF the board could not be read for playing (uiautomator gets no idle state with the moving ambient), so those games were mostly bot-only.
A.suspects:
1. (Strongest) The native-stack transition from game to results runs by the clock while the UI thread is still busy mounting and drawing the results screen.
   - Evidence: frames of 60-150 ms (anim 36-60 ms, draw 36-52 ms, vsync-late 66-78 ms).
   - When the first frame after that stall lands, the transition is already past its start. The old screen is removed in one frame, and the results screen is drawn at partial opacity (hero 50-70%, the rest 0).
   - Seen as a hard cut in 2/5 RM-off runs plus a stalled-then-cut fade in 1/5. In every cut, the gap from mount to first transition frame was 305-857 ms, against 168-269 ms in the smooth runs.
   - If the stall ends while the results hero is still at about 0%, that frame is exactly the reported 'only background' frame. The 'board, EMPTY, board, results' order seen before (fix10, screencap sampling) is consistent with a stalled fade being sampled.
   - Files: measure12-A-rmoff2-cut.png, measure12-A-rmoff3-cut.png, measure12-A-rmoff4-cut.png.
2. The results screen's mount cost lands on the UI thread at the same moment: anim 52-60 ms in the first frame after initGoToTop, then draw 36-52 ms, plus a 100-200 ms background GC. Lowering that cost, or holding the stack transition until the results screen has drawn one frame, would remove the window in which a half-transparent screen can show.
3. Ruled out on device:
   - activity recreation or a root swap: no relaunch or configuration lines;
   - an ambient SurfaceView cycle: no surfaceCreated or surfaceDestroyed, and the ambient digits stay visible in every cut frame;
   - Modals or windows: no window add/remove.
4. Not reproduced with RM ON (0/6, all smooth crossfades). The RM-on path in this build always took 168-269 ms from mount to transition.

B.observations:
Every warp start (8 of 8, both sound settings) creates a NEW full-screen Skia TextureView. logcat shows 'SkiaTextureView: onSurfaceTextureAvailable: 1080x2340' 0.15-0.23 s after the sender's tap. Within 4-8 ms, 'RNSkia: updateAndRelease() failed. The exception above can safely be ignored' follows, and it repeats about 50 times over the 5 s (about one every 100 ms).

The banner and the dim (RN views) reach the screen 66-137 ms after TSA. The brown overlay, which is drawn in that TextureView, reaches the screen 94-348 ms after TSA. It always comes in at full strength in a single frame, because the shared hit clock is already past the fade-in.

Order of the parts:
- First hit: banner first (c1on, c3off), or banner and dim together (c2on, c5off, c6on), or all three at once (c4off). The overlay is never before the banner.
- Second warp in the same game (2 of 2): the dim starts first, 22-34 ms before the banner, and fades in.
- Overlay lag after the banner: 0-211 ms on a first hit, 167-300 ms on a second warp.

The HitRehearsal is visible in logcat about 2.4-3 s after the board: 4 full-screen SkiaTextureViews created 250 ms apart, each with 3-6 updateAndRelease failures. The real warp still creates a fresh TextureView, so the rehearsal does not pre-create the surface the hit uses.

framestats (phone 3, ms):
- The frame that mounts the hit layer: c1on 42.648 draw 27.1, then 42.670 layout 27.6 + RenderThread issue 55.4 (total 153). Similar first frames: c2on 52.256 draw 26.5; c3off 02.864 draw 26.8; c4off 11.878 draw 29.6; c5off 47.383 draw 24.8; c6on 03.613 draw 20.7, then 03.658 total 231.
- Afterwards, for the whole warp: anim 15-48 ms per frame (UI thread), RenderThread issue 12-36 ms, swap 7-13 ms, vsync-late 33-100 ms. End-to-end latency is 55-230 ms. Over the first 1.2 s: 47-58 frames, mean anim 13-16 ms, mean total 49-63 ms, against 11-13 ms totals before the hit. The screen updates every 33-58 ms (20-30 fps) for the whole 5 s.
- The whole screen stalls for 100-170 ms in 3 runs (score stuck on the same number: c3off, c4off, c6on), each time at the moment the overlay first appears.

logcat: no 'Davey!' or 'Skipped frames' from the app, and no GC at any warp start (one NativeAlloc GC at c6on 03.795). Audio: the warp sound starts 28-69 ms before the banner when sound is on; with sound off there is no AudioTrack activity at the hit.

Caveats: the framestats dump ran 1.3-1.7 s after the tap, after the start. 'dumpsys SurfaceFlinger --list' at +0.3 s (c1on) showed no extra SurfaceView, so the warp canvas is a TextureView composited inside the app window.
B.suspects:
1. (Strongest) The warp overlay is a full-screen non-opaque Skia Canvas, which RN Skia backs with a SkiaTextureView. A fresh one is created at every hit, and its first texture updates fail ('RNSkia updateAndRelease() failed', 50 per warp).
   - The RN-view parts (banner, dim, tilt) go up in the commit that mounts the hit layer. The Skia texture shows only when a later frame first succeeds, 1-4 frames later (94-348 ms after TSA).
   - The shared useHitClock started counting at mount, so the overlay (and with it any dim drawn in Skia) appears at full alpha instead of fading in.
   - The second-warp order (dim before banner) shows that the RN-view parts also do not come up in a single frame.
2. The cost of running the effect: UI-thread anim 15-48 ms per frame (Reanimated worklets for the tilt, waves, spiral and banner ring) plus RenderThread issue 12-36 ms to composite a 1080x2340 texture. Together they halve the frame rate for the full 5 s, and that stretches the gap between the parts.
3. The mount frame itself (layout about 28 ms, draw about 27 ms, RenderThread about 55 ms, total about 150-230 ms) produces the 100-170 ms 'whole screen stuck' moments.
4. HitRehearsal does not help with suspect 1: it creates and drops its own 4 TextureViews 2.4-3 s after the board, and the hit creates a new one. Keeping one mounted TextureView (or an opaque/always-mounted canvas, or a SurfaceView like the ambient) would remove the late first texture.
5. Sound itself is not the cause: with sound off (no AudioTrack at the hit) the split and the stall are the same size.

C.observations:
GO! duration (board time minus GO time):
- Joiner, sound ON: 1213-1224 ms without dumps (1489 with dumps).
- Joiner, sound OFF: 2156-2490 ms.
- Host, every run: 1080-1157 ms.

The joiner's time splits into 2 parts:
- (a) GO → game-screen mount: sound ON 0.90-1.18 s, sound OFF 1.84-2.16 s. On the host it is 0.84-0.89 s in all 6 runs.
- (b) Mount → board visible: joiner 306-331 ms, host 227-270 ms.
So the extra sound-off delay (about +1.0-1.3 s) is entirely before the mount.

Sound-off joiner, c3off framestats: dumps 4 (at 45.957) and 5 (at 46.951) are identical ('Total frames rendered: 1216', last frame 45.662). The app window drew no frame at all for ≥1.29 s, from 45.662 until after 46.95. In that gap, logcat shows a burst of about 20 AudioTrack setVolume(0/1/0.3/0.7/0.8) calls (46.157-46.48), the expo-audio players being created. The same burst appears 0.35-0.65 s before the mount in c4off (56.032-56.30) and c5off (31.647-32.03). The video in that period shows only the ambient SurfaceView moving (frames of 65-190 ms).

Sound-on joiners have no such burst under GO. Their players are made in the lobby, and the AudioTrack pairs after the board belong to the hit warm-up. In sound-on runs the UI thread keeps drawing during GO (anim 10-30 ms frames). It then blocks for 222 ms (28.257→28.479), followed by a 144 ms frame (anim 62) and a 104 ms frame (draw 49): that is the game's first draw under GoCover.

The count itself: digits on the two phones are within about ±80 ms of each other. The joiner's '3' is short (734-854 ms), then about 1 s per step. Count sounds lead the visual step by 30-110 ms. Each count step on the joiner also logs 'InputMethodManagerUtils: startInputInner' twice. 'ImeTracker onRequestHide HIDE_SOFT_INPUT_CLOSE_CURRENT_SESSION' comes only after the board, which suggests the join screen's code TextInput is still mounted under the room screen.

Blank frame between the lobby and '3': seen in 12 of 12 count starts, on both phones (not 2 of 4; earlier sampling missed it).
- Joiner: 1 frame (10-21 ms), header 'חדר עם חברים' only, no avatars and no digit, ambient digits visible. The next frame has the full '3' and avatars at full opacity.
- Host: 1-2 frames (11-45 ms), after which the count fades in from 0.
- The lobby frame before it is long: 70-101 ms, a stall while the count mounts.
- logcat in that second: the joiner's startInputInner pair (24.534/24.555 in c1on) and the 'countdownBeat' AudioTrack. No window, surface or relaunch lines.

No JS log lines exist (this release logs only the startup line, which was before the recording windows). No 'Davey!' or 'Skipped frames' from the app.
C.suspects:
1. (Sound-off excess, strongest) GameScreen.tsx line ~1292 calls `useEffect(() => { preloadCues(); }, [])` without checking the sound setting. Meanwhile the lobby warm-up (warmGame.ts warmFriendsGameSteps → soundStep) and warmHitCues skip all players when sound is off.
   - So on a cold-started joiner with sound off, all the game's players (13) are built when the game route mounts, under GO!. Per warmGame.ts, expo-audio builds each one on the UI thread while JS waits.
   - Evidence: zero app frames for ≥1.29 s (identical gfxinfo dumps 4 and 5 in c3off), the AudioTrack creation burst in exactly that gap in 3 of 3 sound-off runs, none in sound-on runs, and the joiner GO→mount of 1.84-2.16 s against 0.90-1.18 s with sound on.
2. (Baseline 1.1-1.2 s on both phones) GO → game-screen mount is 0.84-0.90 s even on the warm host, against the design of GO + 400 ms minus the flow fade. The time passes on the JS side before the game route mounts, while the UI thread is mostly idle. Then the mount and first draw take another 0.23-0.33 s (a 222 ms UI-thread block, a 144 ms frame with anim 62, and a 104 ms frame with draw 49 on the joiner), before GoCover's SWAP_FRAMES and fade. Something between the GO hold (friendsGoHoldMs) and the route push/GoCover 'under' phase waits about 0.6 s more than designed. The JS thread was not observable (no JS logs).
3. (Blank frame) In every count start the lobby content is removed one commit before the countdown content is added (or the count's content mounts at opacity 0 on the host). This is a two-step swap inside the room screen, not a navigation: no window or surface events. It follows a 70-101 ms stall of the lobby frame.
4. (Minor) The join screen's TextInput apparently stays mounted and keeps taking input focus at each count step (startInputInner ×2 per step on the joiner only, IME hide after the board). This adds work on every step of the joiner's count.
